canonical_term: Play to find out what happens
definition: The official statement of Dungeon World's collaborative, open-outcome play principle.
cultural_caution: A table-play principle, not a claim that any published example, actual-play event, or player-created character is fixed canon or a reproducible plot outcome.

supports: The official site describes Dungeon World as a tabletop game and says to play to find out what happens.

definition: Rules procedures described by the official game overview as ways to drive play forward.
cultural_caution: A mechanical procedure triggered by fictional play, not a character class, personality trait, or a guarantee that different tables will narrate the same event.

supports: The official overview defines Moves as ways to drive the game forward.

definition: The GM tool described as keeping the world around players living and evolving.
cultural_caution: A facilitator's planning tool, not a named faction, war, region, or independently canonical timeline. Its details are created for a particular game.

supports: The official overview describes Fronts as helping the GM keep the world around players living and evolving.

definition: The GM guidance term identified by the official overview as keeping facilitation on track.
cultural_caution: A role-at-the-table guide, not a fictional political agenda, an NPC motive, or an instruction to override player consent or boundaries.

supports: The official overview says the GM's Agenda helps keep the game on track.

definition: The official site's stated open license for the text of Dungeon World, allowing attributed derivative use.
cultural_caution: A license is not canon authority. It permits derivative material but does not merge hacks, supplements, actual plays, characters, or campaign events into the original 2012 rules witness.

supports: The official site states that Dungeon World's text is released under a Creative Commons Attribution license and can be used to make/distribute/sell derivatives.
